objectives.understand: Why a written Playbook outlasts any single AI tool, and how a weekly review makes it improve.
objectives.do: Assemble the six Playbook sections from your week's real prompts and re-test two of them.
objectives.demonstrate: Organise prompts into the right sections and choose the right improvement when a prompt underperforms.
objectives.apply: Submit a Playbook that passes the capstone rubric (70 or more).

discover.title: Mission briefing: don't lose the week
discover.scenario: Six days of your best prompts are buried in chat history. Open a new chat and they're gone. Amaka, a bank officer in Lagos, rebuilt the same report prompt from memory three times last month. Today you build the one document that keeps every win: your Personal AI Playbook. It's the capstone, and it counts.

keyIdeas: Six sections: Reports, Emails & messages, Numbers, My-role documents, My privacy rules, My verification checklist.
Weekly ritual, ten minutes: keep what worked and fix one weak prompt.
Tools change; the moves don't. Test new tools against your Playbook, not against hype.

missions.title: File the week's work
missions.prompt: Sort each item into the Playbook section where it belongs.

items.feedback: Your Day 1 template belongs under Reports.
Summaries of long documents sit with Reports.
The email skeleton belongs under Emails & messages.

items.text: 'Never paste payroll, customer names or confidential documents'
items.feedback: This is your privacy card, in your own words.

missions.hint: Each prompt belongs with the kind of work it produces.
missions.support: Ask 'what does this help me make?' A report, a message, a spreadsheet, or a rule for keeping data safe?
missions.explain: Filed by the work it produces, every prompt is findable in seconds. That is what turns a week of chats into a toolkit you keep.

missions.title: Run the weekly review
missions.scenario: During your Friday review you see your customer-reply prompt keeps promising delivery dates you haven't confirmed.

options.text: Switch to a different AI tool.
options.feedback: The problem is the instruction, not the tool. A new tool with the same prompt will do the same.

options.text: Add one sentence to the prompt: 'Never promise a delivery date I have not confirmed; ask me if one is needed.' Save it in the Playbook.
options.feedback: Yes. Fix one weak prompt with one sentence of instruction, and save the corrected version.

options.text: Stop using AI for customer replies.
options.feedback: That throws away a working prompt over one fixable issue.

options.text: Correct each reply by hand every time, and leave the prompt as it is.
options.feedback: That works today, but the problem returns every time. The ritual fixes the prompt once.

missions.hint: The review ritual has three steps. The third is the one that matters here.
missions.support: Look at what went wrong (unconfirmed promises) and find the option that changes the instruction so it can't happen again.
missions.explain: Fixing one weak prompt per week with one sentence is the habit that compounds. The Playbook keeps the corrected version, not the first draft.

advanced.title: Advanced: judge a trending tool
advanced.scenario: Everyone in your office WhatsApp group is talking about a new AI app that 'writes perfect reports'.
advanced.prompt: Which steps reflect today's advice? Select all that apply.

options.text: Test it with two of your own Playbook prompts on real (anonymised) material.
options.feedback: Yes. Your Playbook is the benchmark.

options.text: Check its privacy terms before pasting any work material.
options.feedback: Yes. Your privacy rules travel with you to every tool.

options.text: Run the 4-question check on its output, just as before.
options.feedback: Yes. A new tool doesn't change the need to verify.

options.text: Drop your Playbook and learn the new tool's way of working.
options.feedback: No. The moves (real material, role and format, verify) work in every tool.

options.text: Pay for it quickly before the offer ends.
options.feedback: No. That is hype, not evidence. Test first.

advanced.hint: New tools get tested against your Playbook, not the other way round.
advanced.support: Your Playbook already contains your best prompts, your privacy rules and your checklist. Which options use them?
advanced.explain: Every new tool runs on the same three moves. Testing it with your own prompts, privacy rules and checks tells you in ten minutes whether it is actually better.
